subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an internal rescueWatchdog cron payload and service repair loop after the branch preserves current cron contracts and supplies real host proof?
rationale: The code repair is concrete, but the permanent product and security boundary for a core self-healing service loop needs maintainer intent before this becomes a shipped runtime capability.

options.title: Sponsor after repair and proof
options.body: Keep the PR open, require the current-main contract repairs plus real host recovery proof, and then review the core watchdog direction as an intentional runtime feature.

options.title: Limit to daemon hardening
options.body: Extract only the launchd and abort-signal hardening if maintainers want the security improvements without a core rescue cron feature yet.

options.title: Decline core watchdog
options.body: Close the core feature path if self-healing should remain external/operator-managed until a narrower extension or service API exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, require the current-main contract repairs plus real host recovery proof, and then review the core watchdog direction as an intentional runtime feature.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest current-history signal across the cron, protocol, gateway, and storage surfaces that must be reconciled.
